## Ledger Account

One row of the chart of accounts: `code` (the key every posting uses, such as `1100`), `name`, `type` (one of the account types in `ACCOUNT_TYPES`: `bank`, `ar`, `inventory`, `asset`, `fixed`, `contra`, `clearing`, `ap`, `cc`, `liability`, `longterm`, `equity`, `income`, `cogs`, `expense`, `other`) and `active`. `section` is computed from the type: the statement section the account rolls up to (`asset`, `liability`, `equity`, `income`, `cogs` or `expense`). `cardTitle` is computed as the code followed by the name.

`ACCOUNT_TYPES` is exported beside the card. For each type it gives the label, the statement section and the cash flow activity, and the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow statement all read it.

```ts
import { LedgerAccount } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/accounting/ledger-cards';
```

Posting documents name accounts by their code string (`account: '2000'`), so the Ledger Account card is the reference that gives a code its name, type and section for reports and pickers.

### Operations
None. Accounts are plain reference data.

### Non-goals
No balance is stored on the account; balances are summed from the documents' indexed ledger lines. No parent/child hierarchy or account numbering rules. Documents do not link to the card; they carry the code as text.

### Example
`Account/1100`, Accounts Receivable (type `ar`), the account every invoice debits.
attributes.cardDescription: One account in the chart of accounts: a code, a name, an account type and whether it is active.
